components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他一下子就把作业写完了。
example.pinyin: tā yīxiàzi jiù bǎ zuòyè xiě wán le.
example.english: He finished his homework in no time.
example.fact: A peregrine falcon can dive at speeds over 240 mph (390 km/h), making it the fastest animal on Earth. A hunting stoop lets it close a gap of several hundred meters in just a few seconds — nature's own version of getting something done in no time.

components.note: Simplified from 寫, which originally combined 宀 (a roof) with 舄 (a magpie) — a magpie bringing items into a nest under a roof, an image later extended to the act of putting words down, or 'to write.'
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 她喜欢写作,每天都写日记。
example.pinyin: tā xǐhuān xiězuò, měitiān dōu xiě rìjì.
example.english: She loves writing, and keeps a diary every day.
example.fact: The oldest known writing system, Sumerian cuneiform, emerged in Mesopotamia around 3400 BCE, originally as wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay to track grain and livestock. It took centuries before the same system was adapted to record stories, laws, and poetry.

components.note: Simplified from 無, which originally pictured a person dancing while holding tasseled ornaments (the same image that grew into 舞, 'to dance') — this dance picture was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the negation 'not, without.'
攵 (an action/to strike) — 效 relates to the result produced by an action
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 效's reading xiào

example.hanzi: 这张票已经过期,无效了。
example.pinyin: zhè zhāng piào yǐjīng guòqī, wúxiào le.
example.english: This ticket has already expired and is no longer valid.
example.fact: In 1938, chemist Roy Plunkett was trying to develop a new refrigerant gas when the compound he produced turned out chemically inert and useless for that purpose. The 'ineffective' substance was Teflon, which went on to become one of the most widely used materials in the world.

components.note: 八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 尽管性格不同,他们还是有很多共同点。
example.pinyin: jǐnguǎn xìnggé bùtóng, tāmen háishì yǒu hěn duō gòngtóngdiǎn.
example.english: Despite their different personalities, they still have a lot in common.
example.fact: Dolphins and sharks look strikingly similar — streamlined bodies, dorsal fins, tail flukes — despite dolphins being mammals and sharks being fish that diverged evolutionarily hundreds of millions of years ago. This is a classic case of convergent evolution, where unrelated species independently evolve shared traits because they face the same environmental pressures.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
厂 (a simple shelter or building outline) — 厦 refers to a large building or mansion.
夏 (xià) gives a sound close to shà, sharing the rhyme but differing in the initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 这座大厦有五十层楼那么高。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò dàshà yǒu wǔshí céng lóu nàme gāo.
example.english: This building is as tall as fifty floors.
example.fact: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, completed in 2010, stands 828 meters (2,717 feet) tall, making it the tallest building in the world. Its design was inspired by the geometric patterns of a desert flower, and its structure tapers as it rises to reduce wind loads at the top.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 例 relates to an example or precedent set by a particular case
列 (liè) gives a sound close to 例's reading lì, sharing the same initial consonant and tone
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 每个规则都有例外。
example.pinyin: měi gè guīzé dōu yǒu lìwài.
example.english: Every rule has an exception.
example.fact: The platypus is one of only five living species of monotremes — mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young. Discovered by European naturalists in the late 18th century, it was initially dismissed as a hoax because it broke the rule that mammals give birth to live offspring.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 震 originally described thunder shaking the sky along with a storm.
辰 (chén) gives a sound distantly related to zhèn, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — 撼 relates to an action of shaking or moving something.
感 (gǎn) gives a sound distantly related to 撼's reading hàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 那场地震震撼了整个城市。
example.pinyin: nà chǎng dìzhèn zhènhàn le zhěnggè chéngshì.
example.english: That earthquake shook the entire city.
example.fact: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile, with a magnitude of 9.5, remains the most powerful earthquake ever recorded by modern seismographs. It triggered tsunamis that caused damage as far away as Hawaii, Japan, and the Philippines.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
氵 (water) — 洛 names a river.
各 (gè) gives a sound close to luò, sharing a related rhyme.
囗 (an enclosure) surrounding 大 (a person) — a person resting within a boundary, an image that came to represent 'reliance, cause, reason.'

example.hanzi: 海洛因是一种非常危险的毒品。
example.pinyin: hǎiluòyīn shì yī zhǒng fēicháng wēixiǎn de dúpǐn.
example.english: Heroin is a very dangerous drug.
example.fact: Heroin was first synthesized in 1874 by chemist C.R. Alder Wright, and starting in 1898 the German company Bayer marketed it commercially as a cough suppressant and non-addictive alternative to morphine — a claim that proved tragically wrong once its highly addictive nature became clear.

components.note: An ancient pictograph of a claw-like hand with bent fingers; it was later adopted as the name of the second earthly branch (associated with the ox) and, separately, as a simplified stand-in for 醜, 'ugly.'
阝 (hill/village) — 陋 originally described a rough, out-of-the-way village, extending to mean 'crude, humble.'

example.hanzi: 那只怪物的样子非常丑陋。
example.pinyin: nà zhī guàiwù de yàngzi fēicháng chǒulòu.
example.english: That monster looks very ugly.
example.fact: The anglerfish, found in the deep ocean, is famous for its bulbous body and the glowing lure that dangles from its head, produced by bioluminescent bacteria. Its unsettling appearance is actually a highly effective hunting adaptation in an environment with almost no natural light.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.

example.hanzi: 他的故事深深地打动了我。
example.pinyin: tā de gùshì shēnshēn de dǎdòng le wǒ.
example.english: His story deeply moved me.
example.fact: In the early 1990s, neuroscientist Giacomo Rizzolatti and his team discovered 'mirror neurons' in macaque monkeys — brain cells that fire both when an animal acts and when it merely watches another perform the same action. The finding is often cited as a biological basis for empathy, or being emotionally moved by someone else's experience.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赞 originally related to offering valuables in support of someone.
兟 (shēn) gives a sound distantly related to zàn, having drifted apart over time.
羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'

example.hanzi: 大家都赞美她的勇气。
example.pinyin: dàjiā dōu zànměi tā de yǒngqì.
example.english: Everyone praised her courage.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize was established through the 1895 will of Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, who left the bulk of his fortune to fund annual awards recognizing outstanding achievement. The first prizes, including one for peace, were awarded in 1901.

meanings: one of a sequence of contests

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
亼 (a lid) placed over 口 (a container's mouth) — a lid fitting closed over a vessel, giving 合 its meaning 'to close, join, fit together, unite.'

example.hanzi: 这场拳击比赛一共打了十个回合。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng quánjī bǐsài yīgòng dǎ le shí gè huíhé.
example.english: This boxing match went a total of ten rounds.
example.fact: Heavyweight boxer Rocky Marciano retired in 1956 with a perfect professional record of 49 wins and 0 losses, the only heavyweight champion in history to retire undefeated.

components.note: 亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')

髟 (long hair hanging down) — in its traditional form 髮, this radical shows the character relates to hair; it was later simplified and merged in form with the unrelated 發 ('to send out'), now both written 发.

example.hanzi: 她戴着一头假发去参加派对。
example.pinyin: tā dài zhe yī tóu jiǎfà qù cānjiā pàiduì.
example.english: She wore a wig to the party.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptians, as early as 2700 BCE, wore wigs made of human hair, wool, or plant fiber, both as a fashion statement and to protect their shaved scalps from the desert sun.

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 我昨晚看了一集新的电视剧。
example.pinyin: wǒ zuówǎn kàn le yī jí xīn de diànshìjù.
example.english: I watched an episode of a new TV drama last night.
example.fact: The Queen's Messenger, broadcast live in 1928 on station WGY in Schenectady, New York, is often cited as the first scripted drama ever televised — more than seven years before regular television broadcasting began in the United States.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — melting ice shrinks away, an image linked to 减's meaning 'to decrease.'
咸 (xián) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading jiǎn has diverged.
⺼ (flesh) shows 肥 relates to a bodily state.
巴 (bā) gives a sound distantly related to féi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 为了健康,他决定开始减肥。
example.pinyin: wèile jiànkāng, tā juédìng kāishǐ jiǎnféi.
example.english: For the sake of his health, he decided to start losing weight.
example.fact: Grizzly bears can lose up to a third of their body weight over the winter while hibernating, surviving for months without eating, drinking, or eliminating waste by slowing their metabolism dramatically.

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'
又 (a hand) reaching out to grasp 人 (a person) just ahead — the picture of catching up to someone, giving 及 its meaning 'to reach, to catch up to, in time.'

example.hanzi: 别担心,我们还来得及赶上火车。
example.pinyin: bié dānxīn, wǒmen hái láidejí gǎnshàng huǒchē.
example.english: Don't worry, we can still make it to catch the train in time.
example.fact: Apollo 11's 1969 lunar module landed on the moon with only about 25 seconds of fuel left before mission rules would have required an abort — a margin so tight that astronaut Buzz Aldrin later said the low-fuel warning light was one of the tensest moments of the mission.

components.note: Originally a picture of a woven winnowing basket (the meaning now carried by 箕); the basket shape was borrowed for its sound to write the common pronoun 'its, that, the other.'

An ancient pictograph of a simple shelter or lean-to built around a central pole; this shelter shape was later borrowed for its sound in 餘 ('leftover, surplus'), a meaning modern simplified 余 has inherited directly.

example.hanzi: 我只认识几个人,其余的都不认识。
example.pinyin: wǒ zhǐ rènshí jǐ gè rén, qíyú de dōu bù rènshí.
example.english: I only know a few people; I don't know the rest.
example.fact: British anthropologist Robin Dunbar proposed in the 1990s that humans can realistically maintain stable social relationships with only about 150 people at once — a cognitive limit now known as Dunbar's number. Beyond that circle, everyone else effectively remains 'the rest.'

meanings: degree (to which a situation has evolved)

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'

example.hanzi: 事情已经发展到这种地步了。
example.pinyin: shìqíng yǐjīng fāzhǎn dào zhè zhǒng dìbù le.
example.english: The situation has already developed to this point.
example.fact: Earth Overshoot Day marks the date each year when humanity's demand on nature exceeds what the planet can regenerate that year. In 1970 the date fell in late December; by the 2020s it had crept forward to early August, tracking how far resource consumption has advanced.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — a hand gripping something tightly
丸 (a pebble/pellet) — the small object held firmly in the hand
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 警察每天都在街上执法。
example.pinyin: jǐngchá měitiān dōu zài jiē shàng zhífǎ.
example.english: Police enforce the law on the streets every day.
example.fact: Sir Robert Peel founded London's Metropolitan Police in 1829, creating the first modern professional police force. The 'Peelian principles' he established, including policing by consent rather than force, still influence law enforcement philosophy worldwide.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

example.hanzi: 我星期一要去上班。
example.pinyin: wǒ xīngqīyī yào qù shàngbān.
example.english: I have to go to work on Monday.
example.fact: The seven-day week originated with the ancient Babylonians, who associated each day with one of the seven celestial bodies visible to the naked eye. Monday's name in many European languages, such as French lundi, still honors the Moon.

meanings: to put leftovers in a doggy bag for take-out
(computing) to package (i.e. create an archive file)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'

example.hanzi: 吃不完的菜可以打包带走。
example.pinyin: chī bù wán de cài kěyǐ dǎbāo dài zǒu.
example.english: Food you can't finish can be packed up to take away.
example.fact: The custom of restaurant 'doggy bags' became widespread in the United States during World War II, when food rationing made it socially acceptable, and even encouraged, to take leftovers home rather than waste them.

components.note: 戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'

example.hanzi: 威利是我一个美国朋友的名字。
example.pinyin: wēilì shì wǒ yī gè měiguó péngyou de míngzi.
example.english: Wylie is the name of an American friend of mine.
example.fact: Alexander Wylie (1815-1887) was a Scottish missionary and sinologist who spent decades in Shanghai translating major Western scientific works, including Euclid's Elements, into Chinese, helping introduce modern mathematics and astronomy to 19th-century China.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跳 describes an action done with the feet, jumping.
兆 (zhào) gives a rhyme close to tiào, with the initial and tone shifted.
足 (foot) — 跃 describes jumping or leaping with the feet.
夭 (yāo) is only distantly related in sound to yuè — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 运动员轻松地跳跃过了栏架。
example.pinyin: yùndòngyuán qīngsōng de tiàoyuè guò le lánjià.
example.english: The athlete easily leaped over the hurdle.
example.fact: Fleas can jump up to 200 times their own body length. Their explosive leap is powered not by muscle alone but by a spring-like protein called resilin, which stores energy like a coiled spring and releases it almost instantly.

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 这个地区的电力供应很稳定。
example.pinyin: zhège dìqū de diànlì gōngyìng hěn wěndìng.
example.english: The electricity supply in this area is very stable.
example.fact: In the late 1880s, Thomas Edison and Nikola Tesla found themselves on opposite sides of the 'War of Currents,' debating whether direct current (DC) or alternating current (AC) should power the world. AC ultimately prevailed because it could be transmitted efficiently over long distances.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match

example.hanzi: 退休以后,他过得很自在。
example.pinyin: tuìxiū yǐhòu, tā guò de hěn zìzai.
example.english: After retiring, he lives very comfortably and at ease.
example.fact: Sea otters often sleep floating on their backs on the water's surface, sometimes holding hands with another otter or wrapping themselves in kelp so they don't drift apart during the night — a picture of complete ease and relaxation.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
Simplified from 衛, which originally pictured footprints circling around a settlement (韋) — soldiers patrolling the perimeter of a town, the source of 卫's meaning 'to guard, defend, protect.'

example.hanzi: 士兵们努力保卫自己的国家。
example.pinyin: shìbīngmen nǔlì bǎowèi zìjǐ de guójiā.
example.english: The soldiers worked hard to defend their own country.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China, built and rebuilt across many dynasties starting as early as the 7th century BC, stretches for more than 13,000 miles when all its branches and sections are combined, and was constructed primarily to defend against invasions from nomadic peoples to the north.

meanings: the place where one currently is

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 原 relates to a source high up, such as a spring emerging from rock.
泉 (quán) gives a hint of the sound — 原 is pronounced yuán, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 听到命令后,大家都原地站好。
example.pinyin: tīngdào mìnglìng hòu, dàjiā dōu yuándì zhàn hǎo.
example.english: After hearing the order, everyone stood still in place.
example.fact: A spinning top or gyroscope resists toppling over because of a principle called angular momentum conservation, formally studied by physicist Léon Foucault in the 1850s. The faster it spins, the more strongly it resists forces trying to knock it off its axis, letting it remain upright in place.

components.note: 卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
力 (strength, effort) — 务 relates to exerting effort toward a task or duty, the root of its meaning 'affair, business, to serve.'
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 服务生把菜单递给了我们。
example.pinyin: fúwùshēng bǎ càidān dì gěi le wǒmen.
example.english: The server handed us the menu.
example.fact: Tipping at restaurants is believed to have started in 17th- and 18th-century Europe as a gratuity given 'to insure promptness.' The custom crossed to the United States after the Civil War, though it remains far less common or expected in many other countries today.

components.note: 巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.
丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'

example.hanzi: 这是一个民主国家。
example.pinyin: zhè shì yīgè mínzhǔ guójiā.
example.english: This is a democratic country.
example.fact: Around 508 BC, the Athenian statesman Cleisthenes introduced reforms often credited with founding the earliest known democracy, in which eligible male citizens voted directly on laws and policy in a public assembly.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撤 relates to an action performed by hand, specifically withdrawing or removing something.
钅 (metal) — 销 originally meant to melt metal.
肖 (xiào) gives a rhyme close to xiāo, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 他决定撤销这个决定。
example.pinyin: tā juédìng chèxiāo zhège juédìng.
example.english: He decided to revoke this decision.
example.fact: The 'undo' function in computing traces back to the Bravo word processor, developed at Xerox PARC for the Xerox Alto in 1974 — one of the first applications to let users reverse a mistaken action rather than start over.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宾 describes someone welcomed under one's roof.
兵 (soldier) — a soldier 兵 quartered under one's roof 宀 gave 宾 its meaning 'guest, visitor.'
饣 (food) points to a place where meals are served.
官 pictures an official hall or residence, giving 馆 its sense of a large public building.

example.hanzi: 我们在宾馆住了三天。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài bīnguǎn zhù le sān tiān.
example.english: We stayed at the hotel for three days.
example.fact: The Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, a hot-spring inn in Yamanashi, Japan, was founded in 705 AD and is recognized by Guinness World Records as the oldest continuously operating hotel in the world, having welcomed guests for more than 1,300 years.

components.note: 讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 说来话长,我们还是坐下慢慢聊吧。
example.pinyin: shuōláihuàcháng, wǒmen háishì zuò xià mànman liáo ba.
example.english: It's a long story — let's sit down and talk it through slowly.
example.fact: Leo Tolstoy's War and Peace, published in 1869, runs to roughly 587,000 words across four volumes, making it one of the longest novels ever written. Unabridged audiobook recordings of it typically run over 60 hours.

components.note: 女 (woman) — the semantic side, though the link to 'absurd, reckless' is not obvious today.
亡 (wáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 妄, differing only in tone.
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 他妄想一夜暴富。
example.pinyin: tā wàngxiǎng yī yè bàofù.
example.english: He fantasizes about getting rich overnight.
example.fact: In 1920, Charles Ponzi ran a scheme in Boston promising investors a 50% return within 45 days, paying early investors with money from new ones rather than any real profit. The fraud, now known as a Ponzi scheme, collapsed within months but left his name attached to the tactic ever since.

components.note: An ancient pictograph of a hand holding a forked recording stick, used by scribes and officials to keep records — the origin of 事's meaning 'affair, matter, task.'
力 (strength, effort) — 务 relates to exerting effort toward a task or duty, the root of its meaning 'affair, business, to serve.'

example.hanzi: 他每天都有很多事务要处理。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān dōu yǒu hěn duō shìwù yào chǔlǐ.
example.english: He has a lot of matters to deal with every day.
example.fact: China's imperial civil service examination system, established during the Sui Dynasty around 605 AD, selected government officials based on merit rather than birth, and remained in use for over 1,300 years — one of the earliest large-scale meritocratic administrative systems in world history.

components.note: 令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 这个新药还没有命名。
example.pinyin: zhège xīn yào hái méiyǒu mìngmíng.
example.english: This new medicine hasn't been named yet.
example.fact: Swedish botanist Carl Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature in his 1753 work Species Plantarum, establishing the two-part Latin naming system for species that biologists still use today to name every newly discovered organism.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/wall) — 防 relates to defensive walls and prevention
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 防 is also pronounced fáng, a close match
彳 (step, movement) — 御 relates to travel, as in driving or riding a chariot.
卸 (xiè) gives a sound distantly related to yù's reading, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 城墙是古代重要的防御工事。
example.pinyin: chéngqiáng shì gǔdài zhòngyào de fángyù gōngshì.
example.english: City walls were an important defensive structure in ancient times.
example.fact: France's Maginot Line, an extensive network of fortifications built along its border with Germany in the 1930s, was designed to be a nearly impenetrable defense. In 1940, German forces bypassed it almost entirely by invading through Belgium, rendering the fortifications largely irrelevant.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'

example.hanzi: 导游为我们指引了正确的方向。
example.pinyin: dǎoyóu wèi wǒmen zhǐyǐn le zhèngquè de fāngxiàng.
example.english: The tour guide pointed us in the right direction.
example.fact: Homing pigeons can find their way back over hundreds of miles of unfamiliar terrain, likely relying on a combination of the sun's position, Earth's magnetic field, and even their sense of smell to guide themselves home.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他家院子里种了很多花。
example.pinyin: tā jiā yuànzi lǐ zhòng le hěn duō huā.
example.english: His family's yard has many flowers planted in it.
example.fact: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon, listed among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World by Greek writers, were described as a series of tiered garden terraces rising like a mountain, though archaeologists have never definitively located their physical remains.

components.note: 角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'
攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这项新技术解放了大量劳动力。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng xīn jìshù jiěfàng le dàliàng láodònglì.
example.english: This new technology freed up a large amount of labor.
example.fact: Eli Whitney's mechanical cotton gin, patented in 1793, dramatically sped up the processing of cotton fiber. Rather than reducing the demand for enslaved labor as some hoped, it made cotton farming far more profitable and helped expand slavery across the American South.

components.note: 司 depicts a person with a raised arm giving orders — an official directing others, giving rise to the meaning 'to manage' or 'to take charge of.'
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 司法独立是法治社会的基础。
example.pinyin: sīfǎ dúlì shì fǎzhì shèhuì de jīchǔ.
example.english: Judicial independence is the foundation of a society ruled by law.
example.fact: The French philosopher Montesquieu formalized the idea of separating governmental power into legislative, executive, and judicial branches in his 1748 work The Spirit of the Laws, an idea that heavily influenced the structure of the United States Constitution decades later.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — represents a home.
各 (each, various) — a person arriving from elsewhere and welcomed under one's roof gave 客 its meaning 'guest, visitor.'
广 (a building/shelter) — 厅 names a large room inside a building, a hall.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound close to tīng.

example.hanzi: 我们在客厅里看电视。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài kètīng lǐ kàn diànshì.
example.english: We watch TV in the living room.
example.fact: Television ownership in American households jumped from roughly 9% in 1950 to over 90% by the early 1960s, a shift so rapid that furniture makers redesigned living rooms around the TV set as the new focal point.

meanings: without two sticks to rub together

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

Simplified from 無, which originally pictured a person dancing while holding tasseled ornaments (the same image that grew into 舞, 'to dance') — this dance picture was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the negation 'not, without.'
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.

example.hanzi: 火灾之后,他们一无所有。
example.pinyin: huǒzāi zhīhòu, tāmen yīwúsuǒyǒu.
example.english: After the fire, they had nothing at all.
example.fact: The Great Fire of London in 1666 destroyed an estimated 13,200 houses and left tens of thousands of residents without homes, though historians have also noted it likely helped end a major outbreak of plague by killing off large numbers of rats and their fleas.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 我们已经预定了明天的机票。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yǐjīng yùdìng le míngtiān de jīpiào.
example.english: We've already booked tomorrow's plane tickets.
example.fact: American Airlines and IBM developed SABRE in the early 1960s, one of the first large-scale real-time computer reservation systems. It could process thousands of ticket bookings a day, a radical improvement over the manual card-file systems airlines had used before.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跪 describes an action done with the legs, kneeling.
危 (wēi) gives a sound distantly related to 跪's reading guì, having drifted apart over time.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 士兵在国王面前跪下。
example.pinyin: shìbīng zài guówáng miànqián guì xià.
example.english: The soldier knelt down before the king.
example.fact: Medieval European knighting ceremonies, dating back to at least the 11th century, traditionally required the candidate to kneel while a monarch touched their shoulders with a sword blade — a ritual known as the 'accolade.'

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轮 names the wheel of a vehicle.
仑 (lún) gives the sound — an exact match with 轮's reading lún.
木 (wood) shows 椅 is typically made of wood.
奇 (qí) gives a sound distantly related to yǐ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他因为受伤,不得不坐轮椅。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi shòushāng, bùdé bù zuò lúnyǐ.
example.english: Because he was injured, he had no choice but to use a wheelchair.
example.fact: The first folding, portable wheelchair was patented in 1933 by Harry Jennings and Herbert Everest, whose company, Everest & Jennings, went on to dominate wheelchair manufacturing in the United States for decades.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 软 originally described a cart with cushioned, springy wheels, giving a soft ride.
欠 (qiàn) gives a sound distantly related to ruǎn, having drifted apart over time.
弓 here pictures a young, bent shoot rather than a bow.
冫 (ice/frost) repeated twice suggests two young shoots wilting in the cold, giving 弱 its meaning 'weak, fragile.'

example.hanzi: 面对困难,他从不软弱。
example.pinyin: miànduì kùnnán, tā cóng bù ruǎnruò.
example.english: Facing difficulties, he is never weak.
example.fact: Bamboo can bend dramatically in strong wind without snapping because its hollow, fibrous structure lets it flex and absorb stress rather than resist it rigidly — a property engineers now study when designing earthquake-resistant buildings.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谣 is spread through spoken words.
䍃 (yáo) gives the sound — an exact match with 谣.
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 网上到处都是关于他的谣言。
example.pinyin: wǎng shàng dàochù dōu shì guānyú tā de yáoyán.
example.english: There are rumors about him everywhere online.
example.fact: Orson Welles's 1938 radio dramatization of The War of the Worlds was mistaken by some listeners for an actual news broadcast of an alien invasion, becoming one of the most famous examples in history of a rumor spreading rapidly through mass media.

components.note: 亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 公司这个月来了几个新人。
example.pinyin: gōngsī zhège yuè lái le jǐ gè xīnrén.
example.english: The company got a few new hires this month.
example.fact: Periodical cicadas of the genus Magicicada spend up to 17 years underground as nymphs before emerging as adults all at once — an extreme natural version of a whole cohort of newcomers appearing together after decades unseen.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.
木 (wood) — 构 relates to building structures, originally from wooden framing
勾 (gōu) gives a sound close to 构's reading gòu

example.hanzi: 这栋建筑的结构非常特别。
example.pinyin: zhè dòng jiànzhù de jiégòu fēicháng tèbié.
example.english: This building's structure is very unique.
example.fact: The Eiffel Tower, completed in 1889, was engineered with an open lattice-iron framework specifically to reduce wind resistance. Strong winds pass through the gaps in its structure rather than pushing against a solid surface, which is part of why it has stood for well over a century.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 我常常回想起小时候的事情。
example.pinyin: wǒ chángcháng huíxiǎng qǐ xiǎoshíhou de shìqing.
example.english: I often think back to things from my childhood.
example.fact: Memory researchers have documented a 'reminiscence bump' — a tendency, first studied in autobiographical memory research during the 1980s, for older adults to recall a disproportionate number of vivid memories from their adolescence and early adulthood, roughly between ages 10 and 30.
